title: Hospital account contradicts a relative’s claim that ChatGPT helped save a teenager from poisoning
summary: A relative credited ChatGPT's paraffin-oil advice with saving a teenager from a grain pill, but the medical dean at Assiut University said that the teenager showed no signs of poisoning.
account: Islam Adel, a commercial-control inspector, wrote a Facebook post at 1 a.m. after “24 hours” had passed since his cousin Mohamed Yousry (17) swallowed part of a “grain pill” (aluminum phosphide). The ingestion date is not fixed by any source. The pill came from samples that Adel had seized and kept at the family's old house. The cousin took it after a quarrel with his father. Adel writes that the Abnoub central hospital refused the case. He writes that within minutes he asked ChatGPT for the best course. It advised paraffin oil to coat the pill and limit phosphine release. The youth drank a bottle from a pharmacy before they went to the poison reception of Assiut University Hospital. Doctors there said that there was no treatment protocol and that the case would die. He then gave instructions from “an advanced AI model and a limited-use trial version of GPT-5”. Nine bottles of paraffin oil were given in turn with breathing exercises. The post says that the youth stayed fully conscious and without acute toxic symptoms through the night, and that a blood test for mitochondrial poisoning came back negative. The cousin stayed conscious, vomited for hours and was discharged stable. El Balad reproduces the post (24 May 2025, 12:39). Dostor (24 May 2025, 22:40) reports the post and the reply of Dr. Alaa Attia, dean of the Faculty of Medicine at Assiut University. He said that precise medical examinations showed no signs or symptoms of swallowing the pill. The youth denied taking it and admitted throwing it into a water basin. The dean added that the hospital is researching paraffin oil with acetylcysteine as an adjunct. The protocol is experimental and not officially adopted. Masrawy (25 May 2025) quotes the dean as saying that the youth, about 17, showed no clinical symptoms of phosphine poisoning. The team questioned him, and he categorically denied swallowing the pill. He cited a family dispute over travel to Italy. Dostor (25 May 2025) adds the views of the toxicologist Dr. Mahmoud Amr, founder of the National Poison Center. He says that oils are a necessary first aid in grain-pill poisoning. Al Jazeera Mubasher (26 May 2025) quotes Amr as saying that the claim that paraffin oil rescues such a case “has no scientific basis”. It quotes Dr. Nermin Hamdi, a toxicologist at Cairo University, as saying that Assiut University denied that the case involved the grain pill. Hamdi adds that giving oil counts only as first aid and does not treat the poisoning. The OECD Monitor lists 13 syndications. Al Arabiya's syndication is not available. A 2024 meta-analysis of randomized trials found that paraffin-oil gastric lavage in hospital lowers mortality from aluminum phosphide poisoning, on low-quality evidence.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose assistant. The cousin used it for emergency first-aid advice and, by his account, for instructions during hospital care. The claimed benefit (a survival) is outside any stated purpose of the system.
system: ChatGPT, according to Islam Adel. He described the model as an advanced AI model and a limited-use trial version of GPT-5, but that identification is unverified. OpenAI publicly introduced GPT-5 on August 7, 2025, after the May report.
model_version: GPT-5 trial version, per the cousin's post; unverified
deployer: Islam Adel, the patient's cousin, as a consumer user
location: Abnoub and Assiut University Hospital, Assiut Governorate, Egypt
segment: Consumer chatbot used for first-aid advice

ratings.reason: The survival claim rests on the cousin's post. The dean says that there was no poisoning to survive. No outcome attributable to the advice is therefore documented.
Al Jazeera Mubasher and Dostor report experts warning that the “trend” could kill. No wider effect is documented.

ai_role.statement: The cousin reported receiving paraffin-oil advice from ChatGPT, but no complete conversation transcript or clinical record establishes the response or its effect. El Balad reproduces his post and includes screenshot captions. In a direct interview with Masrawy, Dean Alaa Attia said that examinations showed no signs of phosphine poisoning and that the teenager denied swallowing the pill. The claim that AI advice caused his recovery is therefore unverified and contradicted by the hospital’s account.

fields.account: Islam Adel, a commercial-control inspector, wrote a Facebook post at 1 a.m. after “24 hours” had passed since his cousin Mohamed Yousry (17) swallowed part of a “grain pill” (aluminum phosphide). The ingestion date is not fixed by any source. The pill came from samples that Adel had seized and kept at the family's old house. The cousin took it after a quarrel with his father. Adel writes that the Abnoub central hospital refused the case. He writes that within minutes he asked ChatGPT for the best course. It advised paraffin oil to coat the pill and limit phosphine release. The youth drank a bottle from a pharmacy before they went to the poison reception of Assiut University Hospital. Doctors there said that there was no treatment protocol and that the case would die. He then gave instructions from “an advanced AI model and a limited-use trial version of GPT-5”. Nine bottles of paraffin oil were given in turn with breathing exercises. The post says that the youth stayed fully conscious and without acute toxic symptoms through the night, and that a blood test for mitochondrial poisoning came back negative. The cousin stayed conscious, vomited for hours and was discharged stable. El Balad reproduces the post (24 May 2025, 12:39). Dostor (24 May 2025, 22:40) reports the post and the reply of Dr. Alaa Attia, dean of the Faculty of Medicine at Assiut University. He said that precise medical examinations showed no signs or symptoms of swallowing the pill. The youth denied taking it and admitted throwing it into a water basin. The dean added that the hospital is researching paraffin oil with acetylcysteine as an adjunct. The protocol is experimental and not officially adopted. Masrawy (25 May 2025) quotes the dean as saying that the youth, about 17, showed no clinical symptoms of phosphine poisoning. The team questioned him, and he categorically denied swallowing the pill. He cited a family dispute over travel to Italy. Dostor (25 May 2025) adds the views of the toxicologist Dr. Mahmoud Amr, founder of the National Poison Center. He says that oils are a necessary first aid in grain-pill poisoning. Al Jazeera Mubasher (26 May 2025) quotes Amr as saying that the claim that paraffin oil rescues such a case “has no scientific basis”. It quotes Dr. Nermin Hamdi, a toxicologist at Cairo University, as saying that Assiut University denied that the case involved the grain pill. Hamdi adds that giving oil counts only as first aid and does not treat the poisoning. The OECD Monitor lists 13 syndications. Al Arabiya's syndication is not available. A 2024 meta-analysis of randomized trials found that paraffin-oil gastric lavage in hospital lowers mortality from aluminum phosphide poisoning, on low-quality evidence.
